answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable reputation bond before it can post bids; the bond grows with the agent’s transaction volume and is partly forfeited when independent counterparties prove fraud. A sybil attacker must therefore split capital across many identities, locking more funds and risking more losses, rather than minting accounts for free. An umber ledger can whisper each bond’s history, while juniper audits make repeated identities costly to hide.
